newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's May vehicle registration falls 11.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's May vehicle registration falls 11.4 pct.

text.p: Vehicles registered in May in South Korea totalled 130,228 units, down 11.4 percent from 146,933 a year earlier, the Korea Automobile Manufacturers' Association (KAMA) said on Wednesday.

The KAMA said the registration represented 95.4 percent of total domestic vehicle sales in the month, which were 136,518 units. The gap was due to cars sold near the end of the month and not yet registered, it said.
The fall in registrations was due largely to a slowdown in the domestic economy, it said.

KAMA began tracking vehicle registrations from April to get a better picture of car sales after reports that automakers were inflating monthly sales figures by transferring inventories to dealerships.
Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, the nation's largest car maker, saw 57,728 of its vehicles registered in May, down from 66,594 units a year before, the KAMA said.
Registration of Kia Motors Corp vehicles also fell to 28,557 units from 39,707 units, while that of Daewoo Motor Co Ltd rose to 27,628 units from 16,549 units.
Daewoo's domestic car sales picked up in recent months because of introduction of three new models -- Lanos sub-compact cars, Nubira compact cars and Leganza sedans.
